newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-KLUSENER LEADS SOUTH AFRICA TO MASSIVE 310-6.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-KLUSENER LEADS SOUTH AFRICA TO MASSIVE 310-6.

text.p: A career-best 92 from Lance Klusener helped South Africa to a massive 310 for six in the seventh and final one-day international against Australia on Sunday.
Klusener hit three fours and one six in one Adam Dale over as Australia's attack were put to the sword on a benign Springbok Park wicket.

With Hansie Cronje hitting three murderous sixes in a 65-ball 69 and Daryll Cullinan racing to an undefeated 57 from only 39 balls during the slog, South Africa improved on their previous highest one-day international score against Australia of 284.
However that total -- scored at Centurion Park on Thursday -- was not enough for victory as Australia took a 4-2 lead in the series.

All-rounder Klusener, promoted to open as a pinch hitter, put on 61 in 11 overs with Herschelle Gibbs (29) for the first wicket and then shared a run-a-ball 48-run second wicket partnership with a second pinch hitter, Pat Symcox (26).
But the explosion came in a 109-run third wicket partnership dominated by Cronje. He hit six fours to go with his three sixes before top-edging a catch off Stuart Law.
Klusener's 115-ball innings finally came to an end when he was caught on the square leg boundary looking to add a second six to his seven fours.
Cullinan ensured the momentum was kept up and with Shaun Pollock hitting eight in three balls as the final over from Adam Dale went for 19, South Africa were able to pass the 300 mark.
